mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 0.25% per annum over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.25% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when GDPC1 YoY < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12M MA by > 3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of persistent INDPRO weakness as defined.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST by more than 1% indicates a broad-based fall in demand for goods and housing, which depresses corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline > 1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in CPIAUCSL above 6% combined with a simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS above 0.5% signals an aggressive inflation-fighting cycle, which increases uncertainty and risk premiums, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors seek growth assets.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 6% AND FEDFUNDS > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during months with CPIAUCSL > 6% and FEDFUNDS > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained PAYEMS growth (>0.5% for four months).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in RSAFS below its 12-month moving average by more than 5% for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer savings and spending power, which reduces demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12M MA by > 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of persistent RSAFS weakness as defined.
